_comment: THE INTENDED BOOT CONFIGURATION FOR BOTH NODES. The live file is /var/tmp/vllm-kv-flags/flags.json, which is per-node and NOT in git -- so this committed copy is the reviewable, recoverable source and local-ops/flags-apply.sh is what installs it. Keep them in step.
_why_not_in_flags_py_defaults: flags.py's DEFAULTS carry a deliberate invariant, stated in its own header: an EMPTY FLAGS FILE BEHAVES EXACTLY AS TODAY, every new mechanism off, so a deploy is a no-op until somebody writes a flag. Turning the disk tier on there would break that. The code defaults stay inert; this file is the configuration. The one exception is load_inflight_max, which is a SAFETY bound and belongs in the code default precisely because inert-by-default is correct for it.
_why_store_paused: THE STORE IS PAUSED, AND THE REASON CHANGED ON 2026-10-11 -- READ THIS BEFORE UNPAUSING. It was paused because the store path stalled the stream by ~1.1s (scripts/test-meter.sh section 1 in the vllm-proxy repo: max inter-event gap 1.137s against a 0.102s baseline, A/B/A 1.109 / 0.111 / 1.067). THAT STALL IS FIXED AND VERIFIED: the cause was the manifest flush, not the pump, and with it off the engine core's thread the A/B/A is 0.675 live / 0.607 paused / 0.610 live -- indistinguishable -- with manifest_writes incrementing, so a flush really did fire in the window. The pause therefore stands as a DELIBERATE CHOICE, not an open defect, for two reasons. (1) The verification ran over the WAN with a ~0.6s floor, which would hide the 0.153s index snapshot that is still on the caller's thread; section 1's gate is a flat 1.0s and CANNOT see that residual, so the honest check is reading its printed MAXGAP against 0.102s FROM THE LAN, paired with manifest_writes. (2) manifest_skipped_busy 462 against manifest_writes 109 says 81% of flush attempts are already refused as busy under live store load -- the O(index) cost as back-pressure, which the append-only journal is what fixes. NOTE WHAT THE PAUSE IS NOT ABOUT: the store had 144.1 GB of LIVE exercise on the 2026-10-11 boot (100,990 keys stored, ladder arm B plus the concurrency probe) with zero Xid and zero preemptions. This is a stream-latency decision, not a stability one. The cost of the pause is unchanged and real: the index stops growing, so the tier serves prefixes already on disk and no new ones -- taken deliberately in favour of every request over future restores. disk_restore stays 1: reading back is the prize and costs the stream nothing.
